body:
In North Carolina, painting the outside of a typical 2,000 sq ft home costs about **$2,740 to $7,320** in 2026, or $1.37 to $3.66 per square foot of living area. That is our estimate, built from national prices and what painters in North Carolina actually earn: a median of $21.21 an hour, 11% below the national median of $23.75.

| | North Carolina | National |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Per sq ft of home | $1.37 to $3.66 | $1.50 to $4.00 |
| 2,000 sq ft home | $2,740 to $7,320 | $3,000 to $8,000 |
| Painter median wage | $21.21 an hour | $23.75 an hour |

## North Carolina exterior painting cost by home size

| Home size (living area) | Typical cost in North Carolina |
| --- | --- |
| 1,500 sq ft | $2,055 to $5,490 |
| 2,000 sq ft | $2,740 to $7,320 |
| 2,500 sq ft | $3,425 to $9,150 |
| 3,000 sq ft | $4,110 to $10,980 |

These are typical ranges for a full repaint with normal prep. A small, simple house with sound paint lands near the low end. Two stories, heavy scraping, wood repairs or premium paint push you toward the top. Enter your own home size and any quote you have in the calculator above.

## Prices in North Carolina's largest metro areas

Painter wages are not the same across the state, so neither are prices. Here is the same 2,000 sq ft house in North Carolina's major metro areas:

| Metro area | Painter median wage | 2,000 sq ft home |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Durham-Chapel Hill | $22.37 | $2,861 to $7,628 |
| Raleigh-Cary | $21.81 | $2,804 to $7,477 |
| Charlotte-Concord-Gastonia | $21.59 | $2,782 to $7,418 |
| Greensboro-High Point | $20.13 | $2,634 to $7,025 |

The gap between Durham-Chapel Hill and Greensboro-High Point is $2.24 an hour in wages, which works out to roughly $226 to $604 on this one job. Small towns and rural areas usually sit closer to the lower metro numbers.

## What affects the price in North Carolina

**Siding.** Stucco leads on new homes in the South Atlantic region, which includes North Carolina: it was the most common wall material on new single-family homes started in 2023, at 39.4%, based on Census data analyzed by NAHB. Stucco takes more paint per square foot than smooth siding and is usually sprayed and back-rolled, so stucco houses tend to land in the upper half of the range. Wood and fiber cement siding fall in the middle.

**Weather and timing.** Cold is rarely the problem here; rain and humidity are. Sherwin-Williams says the first 48 hours after painting are the critical drying window, and paint needs dry weather to cure, so a good painter watches the forecast and works around storms. Spring and fall are the easiest seasons. In midsummer, crews often start early and avoid walls in full afternoon sun.

**Prep.** On older houses, scraping peeling paint, replacing soft boards, caulking and spot-priming can take longer than the painting itself. If two quotes are far apart, compare the prep each one includes before you compare the totals. Our [national guide to exterior painting costs](/blog/cost-to-paint-house-exterior/) covers the other price factors in detail.

## Hiring a painter in North Carolina

North Carolina licenses general contractors for larger projects through the NC Licensing Board for General Contractors, which you can search by name, license number or county. A typical exterior paint job costs far less than the board threshold, so for painting-only work, focus on insurance, references and a written scope. Ask every painter for a certificate of liability insurance.

If your house was built before 1978, the old paint may contain lead. North Carolina is one of the states EPA authorizes to run its own Renovation, Repair and Painting program, so painters who disturb old paint there are certified through the state program instead of EPA. Ask to see the certification before work starts.

Get at least two or three written quotes that list the same things: which surfaces, how many coats, which paint line, what prep and repairs, and who cleans up. A quote far below the range usually skips prep or uses fewer coats.

## How we worked out these prices

National data from Angi, reported by NerdWallet, puts exterior painting at $1.50 to $4 per square foot of living area. Angi says labor makes up 75% to 95% of a professional paint job. We took 80% as the labor share and adjusted that part by North Carolina's painter wage compared with the national median, using Bureau of Labor Statistics 2025 wage data:

**North Carolina rate = national rate × (0.2 + 0.8 × $21.21 ÷ $23.75) = national rate × 0.914**

Paint and supplies cost about the same everywhere, so only the labor part moves. Treat the results as a planning range, not a quote. Local demand, the season and each painter's overhead all shift real prices.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much does it cost to paint a 2,000 sq ft house in North Carolina?

About $2,740 to $7,320 for the outside, with most jobs in the middle of that range. In Durham-Chapel Hill expect more, about $2,861 to $7,628.

### Where in North Carolina is exterior painting most expensive?

Of the metro areas above, Durham-Chapel Hill has the highest painter wages at $22.37 an hour, and Greensboro-High Point the lowest at $20.13. Prices follow wages because labor is most of the bill.

### When is the best time to paint a house in North Carolina?

Spring and fall are easiest. You need about 48 hours of dry weather after each coat, so a painter will schedule around rain and avoid walls in full summer sun.

### Do I need a licensed painter in North Carolina?

North Carolina licenses general contractors for larger projects through the NC Licensing Board for General Contractors, which you can search by name, license number or county. A typical exterior paint job costs far less than the board threshold, so for painting-only work, focus on insurance, references and a written scope.
